description: Valero Energy is an oil refiner with operations in the U.S., Canada, Latin America, and Europe. Founded in 1980, the company sells gasoline, diesel, and ethanol through outlets under the Valero, Beacon, Diamond Shamrock, Shamrock, Texaco, and Ultramar brands.

title: Valero Energy

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Petroleum refining company Valero Energy leaped 42 spots in our ranking this year, bringing in $175.7 billion in revenue, a 53% increase over the previous year.

  • In May 2023, Valero announced that Joseph W. Gorder would retire as chief executive officer effective June 30, staying on as executive chairman. R. Lane Riggs, Valero’s president and chief operating officer, succeded Gorder.

  • The company’s refining, renewable diesel, and ethanol segments each reported substantial increases in revenue as of the first quarter of 2023 compared to the year-earlier quarter.

  • Valero’s Port Arthur Coker project, which the company expects will improve its efficiency by converting residual crude oil into useable fuels, was completed in March 2023 and began operations the month after.

  • In April 2023, Valero agreed to pay a $1.2 million settlement to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency after its refinery in Benicia, Calif., violated the federal Clean Air Act.

rankings.itemDescription: Like other oil and gas companies, refining giant Valero Energy enjoyed a snapback in revenue and earnings in 2021 as pandemic lockdowns eased. Valero has launched a number of low-carbon and renewable fuel projects in recent years, and has pledged to reduce emissions from its refining operations 63% from 2020 levels by 2025. The company’s Diamond Alternative Energy has taken some heat from environmentalists, however, for lobbying for renewable fuels over zero-emissions alternatives; Diamond is a plaintiff in a recent federal lawsuit against Environmental Protection Agency regulations designed to encourage the sale of electric vehicles.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The U.S. refining sector was battered in 2020 by lockdowns and travel restrictions, pushing the San Antonio–based refiner to a $1.4 billion loss. That compares with 2019’s $2.4 billion profit. One saving grace came from Valero’s renewable fuels business, which capitalized on the push for low-carbon alternatives to fossil fuels. The company now expects to invest half of its growth capital in renewable diesel. As part of its expansion, last year Valero approved a new diesel plant that is expected to begin operations in 2023.

rankings.itemDescription: As CEO Joe Gorder put it when the company released its annual financial report, Valero faced another “challenging environment for the refining business” in 2019. Net income sank 17% year-on-year, to $2.8 billion, even as refinery utilization was at 96% and the company refined record amounts of oil. The business completed a network of central Texas pipelines and terminals, extending the reach of its vast U.S. shale business deeper inland. Its 2020 growth ambitions suffered a blow in late November when its renewable fuels business stumbled: Two ethanol plants were forced to close temporarily, and additional plants went offline in March 2020, as the coronavirus pandemic destroyed demand for any and all types of energy.
